newsitem.title: ROMANIA: Low interest depresses Bucharest bourse turnover.
newsitem.headline: Low interest depresses Bucharest bourse turnover.

text.p: Turnover on the Bucharest bourse edged lower to 1.1 billion lei on Thursday from 1.6 billion previously in trading again dominated by the two first-tier stocks as investor interest continued to dim.
"With the leu (currency) quite firm, shares are growing rather expensive for the foreign buyer," one trader said.

High-caps Oltchim SA chemical plant and fertiliser maker Azomures SA took a combined 94 percent of turnover. Azomures lost 150 lei to close at 1,200, while Oltchim ended trading 50 lei stronger at 1,100.
Brokers said several elements combined to cap domestic buying.

"Small investors are now looking at bank deposits which yield big returns as a more attractive placement," said one broker. "And institutional buyers tend to concentrate on the heavyweights which boast increased liquidity."
Traders said interest in second-tier stocks was almost absent on Thursday with most shares tracking sideways and seven stocks having no deal.
There was some focus on Carbid SA carbide maker and Policolor SA dye maker, but both stocks moved into negative territory under selling pressure.
The unofficial VAB index showed a 0.2 percent rise on the previous session, while the other independent index, the BIG, fell 1.24 percent.
The VAB index is displayed on VANGUARD.
